_comment: MECHANICALLY CHECKABLE CLAIMS THE PUBLIC WEBSITE MAKES.
devicechain.io lives in a separate repository, and its prose is hand-written. Nothing
in the release pipeline reads it -- a release pushes releases.json and nothing else --
so for three releases the site drifted from the platform unnoticed. An audit against
the tree then found 15 wrong claims, of which only TWO had drifted; THIRTEEN were wrong
when they were written.
That split is why this file exists and why it looks the way it does. A periodic re-read
would have caught the two and none of the thirteen, and would have been skipped by the
second release anyway. What is recorded here instead is every claim the site makes that
a machine can settle against this repository -- so writing a wrong one fails CI on the
PR that changes the underlying fact.
🔴 WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT DO, stated plainly so nobody trusts it further than it goes.
It records what the site is BELIEVED to claim. Nothing here verifies that the site
actually says it -- the HTML is not in this repository and is deliberately not fetched
(a gate that needs the network is a gate that goes red on someone else's bad afternoon,
and one that skips on fetch failure is worse than none). Keeping this file faithful to
the page is a human step, and it is one line on the release-prep checklist.
ADDING A CLAIM. Only add one a machine can settle from this repository. 'The platform
is fast' is not checkable; 'the site names these four connector types' is. If a claim
cannot be expressed as a check below, it belongs in the release-prep read-through
instead, not here as a comment nobody executes.

npm_packages._why: The site names these as installable. If one is renamed or unpublished, an install line on the page stops working.

nuget_package._why: Named on the page as the .NET/Unity SDK.

connector_types._why: The site says outbound connectors publish to MQTT, Kafka, SNS and SQS. A type that is removed, renamed, or newly added makes that sentence wrong in one direction or the other -- note gcp_pubsub is deliberately NOT shipped, and the site must not claim it.

rule_type_count._why: The site says 'Eight kinds of rule' and names them. A count in prose is the most rot-prone thing on the page and the easiest to check, so it is checked rather than dropped. This claim shipped WRONG as 'nine' -- the four WindowMode values are modes for the aggregate type, not types of their own, and counting one produced the ninth.

doc_links._why: Pages the site links by path. A docs page that is renamed or deleted turns a link on the homepage into a 404, and nothing else would notice.
